title: FTC Act section 1: term and removal provisions in Humphrey’s Executor
shortTitle: FTC Act section 1: term and removal provisions in Humphrey’s Executor
summary: The statute combined seven-year terms, political-balance requirements, and removal for inefficiency, neglect of duty, or malfeasance in office.
notes:
The version reproduced in Humphrey’s Executor established a five-member commission, capped membership from one political party at three, used staggered initial terms and seven-year successor terms, and listed specific grounds for removal. The Court treated those grounds as exclusive and read them with the commission’s intended independent expert functions.

The restriction did not make every discharge impossible; it limited discharge to the authorized causes. The assigned discussion does not determine every possible meaning of inefficiency or every removal procedure. This is the historical statutory treatment. Trump v. Slaughter (2026) held the removal restriction unconstitutional, so the provision no longer limits presidential removal of commissioners.
